text:
9 random health and fitness things I wish I'd known younger / in 20s and 30s

"dont overthink it" + simple, boring habits u can stick with + "no days off"

--

1. in a rare W, cheapest + healthiest + best, all happen to be the same

examples: eggs, canned tuna/salmon, lentils, ground beef/turkey, tubs of 0% greek yogurt

frozen vegetables are cheaper, faster (the bags u can toss in the microwave), and healthier than fresh ones. I didn't believe this at first either

but eating "clean" and eating mcdonalds, cost about the same...former may even be cheaper in bulk

2. most ppl in really good shape just have 3-4 staples and eat the same things every day

-a tub of oikos triple-zero greek yogurt is something like 500 cals/100 grams protein. it costs $7. then dump a bunch of blueberries/almonds/bananas in there 

-a can of pink salmon is 100 grams of protein, u can order 12 of them for like $50 on amzn

-a can of lentils is 20 grams of protein, add some olive oil and curry powder and it tastes mediterranean. then add salmon to it + eat it on a piece of sourdough toast

these are about as clean as u can get, u can just eat stuff like that after working out (shit like protein + a sweet potato)...check w LLMs but I wouldnt overthink it

u really dont need all the supplements and protein powders. chances are they'll just make u fat since they dont satiate hunger

if u can get 80% of ur diet to a few staples, and are reasonably active, u can be pretty loose on the other 20% and still stay in good shape

3. mix and match

ask LLMs "what are the 20 healthiest foods" and then just find ways to mix and match those

same for different sauces and spices with ground beef or turkey

dont overthink any of this. never met someone who was overweight from eating too much broccoli or too much pink salmon

its always the ppl who count every calorie ("r u sure u should eat an avocado?" or "isnt olive oil bad" or "eggs have too many calories") and then, understandably, they buckle under the pressure and binge on dogshit

ask someone u know who is in good shape and they'll co-sign this + the notion that shit like ozempic is necessary...none of this is that hard

4. restaurant food is usually horrible for you

it tastes good because: heavy cream, butter, sugar, oils, etc

its not designed around ur health

its designed around, best taste at lowest cost

even stuff that sounds healthy like "beef with broccoli" (americanized chinese), the secret ingredients are always the same, tons of sugar, tons of oil

5. "are you hungry enough to eat an apple"

most eating is just boredom

u learn this from fasting a lot. it shows u how in a typical day, u are eating for non-hunger reasons

good test if ur actually hungry is "are you hungry enough to eat an apple"

if ur actually hungry, it'll be yes. otherwise you're just eating bc ur bored

6. dependence

as u get older u will see guys get into bad relationships and stay in them, solely bc they cannot function as a standalone entity

literally no idea how to use a dishwasher or washer/dryer or how to open an oven, press "450," put a piece of meat or fish on a pan, and then wait 45 mins

a lot of misery can be spared thru what is pretty basic self-reliance...u never want to be stuck in a bad relationship bc u dont know how to do fuckin laundry

this is way more common than u would think

7. means and ends

u will see people who get overly vain and optimize everything around health/working out

there's nothing wrong w this per se, but to them, this represents the end

whereas all this shit should really be thought of as, means to an end.

u want a sound body & mind so that u can achieve ur goals - whatever ur goals may be.

8. the fine line between self-actualization and self-indulgence
 
related, but focusing ur entire daily routine and ur life on things like "I must reach 8.7% body fat"... is prob a sign u have gone too far into vanityland

there's a very fine line where u go from health-conscious and disciplined, to "overly self-absorbed narcissist dork"

ur better off thinking in loose goals -- like, "I want to be as muscular as I can, while still being able to see my abs," and "be able to fireman carry a grown man out of a building," and "never have issues helping a friend move."

shit like that

"dont overthink it" is for lifting also, theres like 5 compound movements that carry 90% of the load...pull ups, pushups, squats.  simpler = better = more likely u are to stay with it (applies for everything)

if Father Time will eventually destroy it - like obsessing over body fat % or most 1RMs - its prob not a worthy LT goal and is just driven by vanity....wasting too much of ur life for one IG photo

9. "what you eat at 30, u pay for at 45"

there's a pretty steep exponential decline that u will see between those ages, for the ppl who do everything wrong

exponential in that, the deeper into that pit u get, the harder it is to get out

once you pick up excess fat and stretchmarks and all that, they hang around, compared to ppl u see who were consistently hitting the gym

u cant avoid shit like face wrinkles + receding hairline, but u can 100% dodge the reaper from the neck down, and be 50-60 but have a body that looks half that age

--

TL;DR everything compounds

cliche, but cliche for a reason, bc its true

dont overthink it. trying to be 100% perfect on all the shit u read, will lead to failure -- versus getting to 80-90% on things u can actually stick with

all just means to an end. ur LT goals are what matter, this shit is always best viewed thru that lens

good luck...simple, boring, sustainable habits, plus "no days off," will take u a long way.
